meta.title: Blank Slate Felons
meta.logline: Kindleton's bike thief walks free for the forty-first time, while Dale stops a robbery and gets sentenced to Masculinity Unlearning.
meta.focus: Book chapter 4: criminals recast as victims, recidivism, pathologizing heroic masculinity.
meta.source: Ideas from 'Suicidal Empathy: Dying to Be Kind' by Gad Saad (2026), plus published criticism of the book (The Bulwark, Quillette).
meta.disclaimer: Parody and commentary for adults. Strong language. Original characters. Not affiliated with any author, network or show.

lines.text: Kindleton's beloved bike thief, Slick Vinnie, was arrested today for the forty-first time. He was released for the forty-first time ten minutes later.
He has already stolen the judge's bike. And mine. I walked here, folks. In these shoes.

sequence.ticker: BIKE THEFTS UP 900% • BIKE THIEF SELF-ESTEEM ALSO UP • BICYCLE OWNERS TOLD TO REFLECT ON THEIR PRIVILEGE

lines.text: Mister Vinnie, you've stolen four hundred bicycles.
Your honor, I had a very difficult childhood. My dad never let me ride his bike.
Oh, you poor thing. Case dismissed! Here, take my bike.
Thanks, judge. I'll take the bailiff's too.
This is the dumbest courtroom on Earth.
Penny! That's very punitive language. Mister Vinnie is a justice-involved cyclist.
Saad quotes a grim number. Nearly a third of American male prisoners had been locked up five or more times before.
Treat the offender only as a victim of society, and the actual victims become a footnote. Usually a footnote without a bike.
Vinnie has a punch card. Steal nine bikes, the tenth is free.
Nice wheelchair, grandpa. I'll take it. With you in it, for resale.
Hey! Not today, you slippery little creep!
Ow! He touched me! Somebody call my therapist!
Local hero Dale Doormat, who stopped a robbery today, has been charged with toxic masculinity in the first degree.
Mister Doormat, you used your body to stop a crime. That's very aggressive.
He was stealing a wheelchair. With a guy in it!
I sentence you to six weeks of Masculinity Unlearning. You will cry on cue, apologize to furniture, stop holding doors, because that's benevolent sexism, and never, ever open a jar.
Not the jars!
Three weeks of unlearning, Rocco. I cried at a parking ticket. I apologized to a hedge. The hedge did not accept.
*sympathetic chitter* (steals Dale's wallet)
Saad's complaint: we used to cheer the man who ran toward danger. Now we pathologize him, and applaud the bloke tweeting a sad face from a safe distance.
His evidence is romance novels. Goodreads has a list called All Time Dominant-Alpha Romance Heroes. There is no list for sensitive betas who cry at Sleepless in Seattle.

And zoology has a term for the alternative. Kleptogamy. Colloquially, the sneaky fucker. A male who mimics a female to slip past the big fellow and get at the ladies. Saad's point: performing harmlessness is a strategy, not a virtue.
I'm eleven.
He leans on a real New York subway case, where a Marine restrained a man who was threatening passengers, the man died, and the Marine was charged. It's still argued about bitterly.

sequence.title: HEART vs HEAD
sequence.sub: Tonight: villains, victims and very tired juries

lines.text: Tonight on Heart versus Head: who deserves our sympathy, the criminal or the victim? I'm going to say the guy whose bike got stolen. Me. I'm the victim.
Hal, the heroic vigilante story has a dark side. Sometimes the hero misjudges the situation, and somebody dies. That subway case is not a cartoon.
True, and courts should look hard at cases like it. But there's a difference between investigate the man who stepped in, and assume he's the villain.
And rehabilitation isn't fluff. Education and job programs inside prison really do cut reoffending.
Agreed! Rehab for people who want it. Consequences for bike number forty-one.
Compassion for offenders. But victims first.
Programming note: the courthouse sign has just been stolen by Slick Vinnie.
Your honor, my motion is simple. Some empathy for the victims. All four hundred of them.
Hmm. I never considered the bikes' feelings.
The people, Judge. The people who own the bikes.
Mister Vinnie, you will repair every bike you stole. And there's a job at the bike shop, if you show up on time.
A job? Like, with mornings?
Tit for tat, sweetie.
Penny, look! I opened a jar! I am a man again!
*chomp chomp* (eats the entire jar)
Rehab is going great.
